Add an element with the referenced id, or update the fragment link to point to an existing target.

Treat public env prefixes as publication, not secrecy; keep secret env vars server-only and rebuild after rotating leaked keys.
Remove the secret from client bundles/static assets, rotate it, and route privileged service calls through server-only code.
Don't persist auth tokens (JWTs, access/refresh tokens, secrets) in `localStorage`/`sessionStorage`; they're readable by any XSS. Use an `HttpOnly` cookie set by the server.
Use a valid autofill token in `autoComplete` so browsers can fill the right field reliably.
Give every Base UI Dialog.Popup and AlertDialog.Popup a Title part (visually hidden when the design shows no heading) or name the dialog with aria-label.
Give every Field.Root that wraps a Field.Control a Field.Label (visually hidden when the design shows no label) or name the control directly with aria-label.
Render each Base UI Tabs.Tab inside Tabs.List so the tablist role and arrow-key focus handling cover every tab.
Run dependency installs with scripts disabled before exposing secrets, isolate untrusted build code, and move signing/deploy authority into a narrow privileged step.
Set an explicit button `type` so plain buttons do not submit forms by accident: `type="button"`, `"submit"`, or `"reset"`.
Add `onChange`, `readOnly`, or `defaultChecked` so React knows whether the checkbox is editable, display-only, or uncontrolled.
Release listeners and timers acquired in `componentDidMount`/`constructor` by adding a `componentWillUnmount` that removes them (or use MobX `disposeOnUnmount`).
Pair `onClick` with a key handler so keyboard users can trigger it.
Allowlist redirect origins/paths, set `frame-ancestors` for privileged pages, and avoid URL-prefilled privileged dialogs.
Avoid shell execution for caller-controlled values. Use fixed commands, argument arrays, strict allowlists, and no shell interpolation.
Give every interactive control a label screen readers can read.
Keep auth cookies host-only and HttpOnly, avoid credentialed CORS for less-trusted docs/vendor origins, and isolate documentation domains from app sessions.
Prefer rendering structured React nodes. If HTML is required, sanitize with a well-reviewed sanitizer and keep the trust boundary close to the sink.

A debounced/throttled callback holds a pending timer that still fires after unmount, so add `useEffect(() => () => debounced.cancel(), [debounced])` to cancel the trailing invocation when the component tears down.
Give every `<dialog>` / `role="dialog"` an accessible name with `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` (referencing the dialog's title element).
Extract a shared component when the repeated JSX trees represent the same UI concept and should evolve together.
Pass the same callback binding and capture flag to `addEventListener` and `removeEventListener`, or abort the registration's local AbortController during cleanup.

Removal APIs match by reference identity, so the second inline function passed to the remove call can never equal the one you added; hoist the handler into a single named const (or useCallback) and pass that same reference to both the add and remove calls.

Return a cleanup function that calls `observer.disconnect()` (or `observer.unobserve(node)`) so the observer stops firing callbacks against detached nodes after unmount instead of leaking on every mount.
Store the frame id and return a cleanup that calls `cancelAnimationFrame(id)` so self-scheduling work cannot continue after unmount.
Read env vars with static dotted access (`process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_NAME`). Computed access and destructuring aren't inlined by babel-preset-expo and resolve to `undefined` at runtime.
Derive authority fields on the server or enforce them in Firebase/Supabase rules; never trust client-provided owner, org, or role values.
Bind every read/write to `request.auth.uid`, immutable ownership, and tenant membership instead of treating sign-in as authorization.
Configure blocked DOM props so plain HTML tags stay on the agreed DOM API surface.
Configure blocked elements so code stays on the approved UI primitives.
Accept the `ref` parameter or drop `forwardRef` so parents are not promised a ref that never reaches the node.
Validate owner, repo, org, and branch identifiers against strict slugs and build URLs with URL/path encoders instead of raw interpolation.
Put readable text in every heading.
Set `<html lang="…">` so screen readers know the page language.
Associate each label with one native control; use fieldset and legend to name a group of controls.

Swap the `

Put each table element in its required parent: `<thead>`/`<tbody>`/`<tfoot>` directly inside `<table>`, `<tr>` inside a row group, `<td>`/`<th>` inside `<tr>`. Browsers quietly fix broken table markup, so write it to spec.
Keep forms separate, or make the inner action a button associated with the outer form. HTML does not permit form descendants inside a form.
Move the inner control beside its interactive ancestor so each action has independent semantics and focus behavior.
Add a descriptive `title` so screen reader users know what the embedded frame contains.
Add `sandbox=""` or a curated value so embedded pages cannot get full access to your site by default.
Do not put 'image' or 'photo' in alt text. Describe what is shown.
Parse imported metadata as data with strict schemas; do not evaluate EXIF, manifests, presets, dropped files, or archives.
Pass `{exitOnCtrlC: false}` to `render()` before handling Ctrl-C with `useInput`.
Use Ink's `useApp().exit()` so Ink restores terminal state.
Move `useStdin().setRawMode()` to an effect and restore it in cleanup.
Use Ink primitives such as `<Box>` and `<Text>` instead of DOM host elements.
Use React Router's memory router APIs in Ink applications.
Move focus-manager calls to an effect or input handler.
Move Ink layout components outside `<Text>` and `<Transform>` boundaries.
Keep input subscriptions out of components used only by `renderToString()`.
Measure Ink elements in a layout effect, effect, callback ref, or event handler.
Combine unconditional output in one render root into a single `<Static>`.
Wrap terminal text in Ink's `<Text>` component.
Call Ink `render()` once and update or rerender the returned instance.
Use Ink's shared `useAnimation()` scheduler and automatic unmount cleanup.
Pass `<Static>` a collection whose existing entries never reorder or disappear.
Put a stable `key` on the root element returned by `<Static>`.
Use Ink's `useWindowSize()` so resize events trigger a render.
Measure terminal columns with `string-width` before calling `setCursorPosition`.
Run inherited-TTY child processes inside `useApp().suspendTerminal()`.
Use a role supported by Ink and do not label elements hidden from screen readers.
Use modern primitives, `crypto.randomBytes` / Web Crypto randomness, and timing-safe comparisons for signatures, digests, tokens, and auth material.

Set auth/session cookies server-side with `httpOnly: true`, `secure: true`, and `sameSite`. Cookies set via `document.cookie` or with `httpOnly: false` are readable by any XSS payload and can be stolen.
Add keyboard focus support so users can reach interactive elements without a pointer.
Split it into one derived atom per field (each compares cleanly with Object.is), or wrap with `selectAtom(source, fn, shallow)` from jotai/utils if you really need one object.
Lift `selectAtom(base, fn)` to module scope, or wrap it: `const atom = useMemo(() => selectAtom(base, fn), [deps])`. Calling it during render makes a new atom every time and re-subscribes forever.
Derive the field you read: `const dataAtom = atom((get) => get(queryAtom).data)`. Subscribing to the whole query atom re-renders on every refetch, focus, or no-op cache hit.
Await the accumulator first: `const acc = await previous; ...; return acc;`. Seed it with `Promise.resolve(initial)` so the first run also gets a Promise
Add a stable `key` prop so React can keep list items matched to the right data when the list changes.
Wrap JSX comments in `{/* … */}` so users do not see comment text rendered as children.
Wrap the context value in `useMemo` or move it outside the component so consumers do not redraw every render.
Remove or rename one of the duplicate props so the later value does not silently override the earlier one.
Move the JSX outside the component or wrap it in `useMemo` so memoized children do not redraw every render.
Wrap the array in `useMemo` or move it outside the component so memoized children do not redraw every render.
Wrap the callback in `useCallback` or move it outside the component so memoized children do not redraw every render.
Wrap the object in `useMemo` or move it outside the component so memoized children do not redraw every render.
Use real event handlers instead of `javascript:` URLs so injected URL text cannot execute as code.
Add `rel="noreferrer"` (or `"noopener"`) when using `target="_blank"`.
Import the component or fix the typo so React can resolve the JSX identifier at runtime.
In `{items.length && <List/>}` React renders a literal `0` when the count is 0. Compare explicitly (`items.length > 0 && <List/>`) or use a ternary (`items.length ? <List/> : null`).
Spread each value at most once so later props cannot silently override earlier props from the same object.
Never accept the `none` algorithm; it disables signature verification and lets any forged token through. Pin the real algorithm(s) explicitly (`jwt.verify(token, key, { algorithms: ['RS256'] })`).
Remove private keys from source, rotate exposed credentials, prefer short-lived deploy credentials, and document revocation/expiry for release keys.
Tie every label to a control with `htmlFor`, or by nesting the input.
Use a valid language code like `en` or `en-US` so screen readers choose the right pronunciation rules.
Use exact origin allowlists after URL parsing, per-request nonces, narrow methods, and never expose install/update commands to arbitrary web pages.
Use a constrained compiler for untrusted content, disable expressions/raw HTML, sandbox renderers, and avoid caching attacker-controlled output across tenants.
Add `<track kind="captions">` inside every `<audio>` / `<video>`.
Replace inheritance with composition, or annotate inherited members explicitly with `makeObservable`.
Pass the component directly to `observer`, or apply React `memo` outside the resulting observer component.
Keep the disposer returned by `reaction` or `autorun` and invoke it during teardown.
Keep AnimatePresence mounted and place the condition around its child so Motion can observe and animate the child leaving.
Give every direct AnimatePresence child a stable key derived from its identity so Motion can track which element exits.
Render one direct child at a time in `mode="wait"`, or use `sync` or `popLayout` when several children can be present.
Create Motion components at module scope, or memoize a genuinely dynamic component factory so its identity remains stable.
Constrain horizontal drags with left or right bounds and vertical drags with top or bottom bounds, keeping paired bounds in ascending order.
Start imperative animations from an effect or user interaction, and derive render output declaratively from props and state.
Provide one transition time for each keyframe so Motion can place every value on the animation timeline.
Use inline-block, block, flex, or grid so the browser can apply Motion's transform-based layout animation.
Derive repeated layout IDs from stable item identity, or scope each repeated component with a LayoutGroup ID derived from the item.
Give useTransform input and output ranges the same number of entries so every input stop has an output value.
Use useMotionValue inside React components, or create a manual motionValue outside the render path.
Subscribe with useMotionValueEvent, or create the subscription in an effect and return its cleanup function.
Pair mouse events with keyboard ones so keyboard users are not left out.
Use the same preferred page URL for alternates.canonical and openGraph.url so search and social previews identify one page.
Do not use `accessKey`. It conflicts with assistive tech shortcuts.
Remove `aria-hidden` from focusable elements, or stop them being focusable, so keyboard users do not land on content screen readers hide.

An optional chain is `undefined` when it short-circuits, so `*`/`/`/`%` on it produces `NaN`, which silently corrupts formatting and comparisons. Provide a `?? fallback` or guard the chain root before the arithmetic.
Use a stable id from the item, like `key={item.id}` or `key={item.slug}`. Index keys break when the list reorders or filters.
Keep `role="status"` polite. Use `role="alert"` only when an interruption is genuinely imperative.
Don't make the effect callback `async`. Define an async function inside the effect and call it, then return a real cleanup function if you need one.

An async onClick/onSubmit handler on a host control that awaits a mutating request and sets state only afterward stays interactive across the await, so a double-click fires the write twice. Add a leading `if (busy) return` guard, or set a flag before the await inside `try` and reset it in `finally` while the control is disabled.
Do not use `autoFocus`. It disorients users on load.
Always pair `autoPlay` with `muted` (and `playsInline`): `<video autoPlay muted loop playsInline />`. If the sound matters, drop `autoPlay` and let users start it.
Allow paste so people can use password managers, verification codes, assistive tools, and copied text without retyping it.
Compare against each value separately (or use an array `.includes(x)`) instead of an all-literal `||`/`&&` chain, which short-circuits to its first literal and drops the rest.
Choose either stiffness/damping/mass or duration/bounce for a Motion spring so every configured value takes effect.
Drive the input's `value` from state (`const [value, setValue] = useState(...)`) that `onChange` updates, or drop `value` if the field is meant to be read-only.
Move `createContext(...)` outside the component, to the top level of the file, so it stays the same on every render.
Create object URLs in an effect or event handler and revoke each URL when it is replaced or no longer needed.
Replace `createRef()` with the `useRef()` hook inside function components and hooks. `createRef` is only for class components.
Create stores at module scope so subscribers are not cut off and saved state does not reset every render.
Use either `children` or `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` so React does not ignore one source of content.

`KeyboardEvent.keyCode`/`which`/`charCode` are deprecated and layout/engine dependent for character keys. Branch on `event.key` (logical key like `'/'`) or `event.code` (physical position) so the handler works across keyboard layouts and browsers.
Setting state in `componentDidMount` triggers an extra render. Use `getDerivedStateFromProps` or initial state instead.
Setting state in `componentDidUpdate` causes another render and can loop. Use `getDerivedStateFromProps` instead.
Don't change `this.state` by hand. `setState()` overwrites it anyway, so always go through `setState()`.

Call the setter with a brand new value instead: `setItems([...items, newItem])`, `setItems(items.filter(x => x !== target))`, or `setItems(items.toSorted(...))`. React only redraws when the value is new, so changing it in place does nothing.
Replace `<marquee>` and `<blink>` with normal markup so motion does not distract or disorient users.
Don't use `document.write()`/`document.writeln()`. Append DOM nodes or set `innerHTML`/`textContent` on a specific element instead.
Move the value inside the hook body and depend on its simple inputs instead, or wrap it in useMemo / useCallback so it stays the same between renders.

A custom effect wrapper must return its forwarded EffectCallback's result so React can run the cleanup. Calling it as a bare `fn()` instead of `return fn()` silently drops the cleanup, leaking every subscription/timer/listener it set up.

Bail on IME composition before acting on Enter: `if (e.nativeEvent.isComposing) return;` (or track composition with `onCompositionStart`/`onCompositionEnd`). Otherwise Enter fires mid-composition and commits a half-typed value for CJK users.
Use `JSON.parse` for data, or rewrite the code so it doesn't build and run code from strings.
Use a data-fetching layer or Server Component so fetches do not race, double-fire, or leak from `useEffect`.

After `.fill(value)` every element is identical, so a lone `.map((n) => ...)` binds `n` to that value (whatever the parameter is named) and gives every child the same key. Add the index as the second parameter: `.map((_, index) => ...)`.
Use a ref to reach DOM nodes because `findDOMNode` was removed in React 19 and can crash the app.
A `.then()` chain with no `.catch` in an event handler becomes an uncaught promise rejection no error boundary can catch; add a `.catch` handler (or make the handler `async` and `try/catch`).
Remove focusable descendants from aria-hidden content, or hide and disable the whole subtree together.
Render the same initial output on the server and client, then switch after mount or use useSyncExternalStore with a stable server snapshot.
Don't combine `loading="lazy"` with `fetchPriority="high"`. A high-priority image (usually the LCP) should load eagerly; a lazy image is by definition not high priority.
Keep state updater callbacks pure and return only the next state. Move notifications, storage, timers, ref writes, and other external work into the event or effect that queues the update.
Assign the checkbox element's `indeterminate` DOM property, usually through a ref, because the HTML attribute does not control its visual state.
Do not give an interactive element a role that says it is not interactive.
Keep determinate progress values within a valid positive range so visual and assistive feedback report the same advancement.
`isMounted` doesn't work in modern React. Track mount state with a ref, or cancel the async work instead.
Replace `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value))` with `structuredClone(value)`. It is faster and preserves Dates, Maps, Sets, and cyclic references.

Move `componentWillMount` work to `componentDidMount`, `componentWillReceiveProps` to `componentDidUpdate` or the static `getDerivedStateFromProps`, and `componentWillUpdate` to `getSnapshotBeforeUpdate` plus `componentDidUpdate`. The `UNSAFE_` prefix only hides the warning. React 19 removes both.

Swap `childContextTypes` + `getChildContext` for `const MyContext = createContext(...)` and `<MyContext.Provider value={...}>`. Swap `contextTypes` for `static contextType = MyContext` or `useContext()` in a function component. Move the provider and every consumer together, or some consumers read the wrong context.

A trailing `setLoading(false)` after an `await` never runs if the awaited call rejects, so the flag stays stuck truthy; reset it in a `finally` block (or mirror the reset on every catch) so it clears on both paths.

Format locale/timezone-dependent values in a post-mount useEffect + state, or pass an explicit locale and timeZone so the server and the browser render the same text. Only runs on SSR-capable projects.
Prefer CSS media queries for layout, or subscribe with `useSyncExternalStore` and provide a stable server snapshot.
Use either width descriptors with sizes or density descriptors throughout one srcSet, never both.
Keep one visible main landmark per rendered view so assistive-technology users can jump to the primary content unambiguously.
Give each coexisting navigation landmark a concise, unique aria-label or aria-labelledby value.

Read mutable values like `location.pathname` or `ref.current` inside the effect body, or subscribe with `useSyncExternalStore`. Changing them doesn't redraw the screen, so listing them in deps won't make the effect run again.
